title: Auditing Regulatory Compliance
summary: How to audit the firm's compliance framework and its adherence to regulatory requirements, including the compliance function itself, regulatory reporting and the management of regulatory change.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to audit the firm's compliance framework and its adherence to regulatory requirements, including the compliance function itself, regulatory reporting and the management of regulatory change.
Learning Objectives: Plan audits of the compliance framework and compliance monitoring
Test the accuracy and controls behind regulatory returns
Evaluate how the firm identifies and implements regulatory change
Syllabus: Auditing the compliance function: mandate, resources and monitoring programme
Regulatory reporting: data lineage, reconciliations and sign-off
Regulatory change management and obligations registers
Breach identification, recording and notification to the authority
Intended Audience: Heads of internal audit, audit managers and auditors in banks, insurers, investment firms, fund managers and payment firms
Co-sourced and outsourced audit providers delivering assurance to regulated firms
Audit committee members and compliance and risk staff who rely on internal audit work
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of internal audit, risk or compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No specialist technical background is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Internal Audit Function in Banks (2012)
Institute of Internal Auditors, Global Internal Audit Standards (2024)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
